findings.title: Hyphenation alone does not establish equivalent speech
findings.problem: scriptCompounds treats every alphabetic hyphenated pair as equivalent to its closed spelling. A hyphen can distinguish different words and pronunciations: "re-signed" means signed again, whereas "resigned" means quit. The new normalization erases that distinction, allowing a recording with different meaning through the exact-word accuracy gate.
findings.failure_scenario: audioCheck("The nurse re-signed after the audit.", "The nurse resigned after the audit.") returns pass: true with similarity 1. Both sides become "nurse resigned after audit", although the narration changes the nurse's action.
findings.fix: Restrict folding to explicitly vetted spelling equivalents, including the required meal-time/mealtime and iso-osmolar/isoosmolar variants, rather than deriving equivalence from every hyphen. Add a passing faithful baseline and a failing re-signed/resigned regression test. When tightening this rule, bump QA_VERSION so recordings accepted by the permissive rule are rechecked.

assessment: One accuracy-gate defect remains in compound normalization. The added tests cover the intended spelling variants but miss hyphenated forms whose closed spelling is a different word. I could not independently verify the refreshed visual-review signatures or the provenance of their new sourceKey from the supplied files.
